verdict.tagline: Endless exploration fights a broken technical backbone and relentless updates.
for_you_if: you love sprawling open-world exploration and side quests
you enjoy building and managing intricate settlements
you can overlook a weak main narrative
not_for_you_if: you rely heavily on community mods that survive updates
you want a deep and flexible dialogue system
you need stable performance without long loading screens
you are sensitive to frequent game crashes and bugs

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the main story as weak or forgettable, contrasting it with enjoyable exploration and side activities.

citations.review_text: Picked up Fallout 4 on a Steam sale as I always heard great things about the series but unfortunately I think the series isn’t for me. The story sucked me in right away but immediately lost me as things seemed like they should’ve ramped up, it may be the  story structure combined with the open ended exploration of the game that I am not usually a fan of. The combat feels like a generic fps with way too little ammo available for what the combat asks of you after the intro. I will say the music was really good, environments were well designed and the amount of dialogue options paired with different responses as well as good voice acting are all great qualities of this game. After trying Elder Scrolls for the first time and really loving those I was hoping Bethesda’s other flagship title would impress me again, but ultimately I can’t see that happening even if I put more time in to see how it expands on its early game ideas.
Don't play the story, it sucks. but the gameplay is the best in the series

i only played new Vegas before this and i think fallout 4 is completely different from it. its like developers want player just have fun and explore the world. main story is very forgettable instead I was doing random things like exploring and killing bad guys. A fun game you can play anytime.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the dialogue system as limiting, noting that chosen options do not match the spoken lines or lead to identical outcomes.

citations.review_text:
This is neither a shooter, nor a role-playing game.
Bullet-sponge enemies, nonsense weapons (I'm not talking about Assault Rifle, I didn't get that far). 
Imagine a version of Skyrim where you only come across enemy archers if you yourself play as one. That's how "upgrade system" works here - and the weapon pool is largely reliant on it. Without your perks and levels, new weapons don't exist anywhere in the world!
On Normal difficulty, a standard zombie takes 5 point-blank shots from an early-game shotgun (that holds 2 rounds). Weapon animations are bad - more so than "F4 weapons are bad" videos would have you believe. You will have to watch that stupid revolver cylinder spin EVERY time you pull it out.

The dialogue [i]writing[/i] is fine. But the dialogue [i]system[/i] is not. You can't know what it is you're picking in the dialogue - I went with a polite "we're not friends" only to hear my "character" go "You're pathetic, you're nothing to me". 
And half the time, when you meet some "main quest" stuff, your dialogue options are "agree/agree vigorously/agree, but quirky".
Leveling system is abysmal, they sucked all joy from it. You no longer have Skills, attributes are now upgradeable, and Perks that are FUN are replaced with Perks that are equivalent to Skills (such as "do 20% more damage with pistols, can upgrade this 5 times". That's not what a perk is, you know?).

Play this if you're ready to mod the game to make it vaguely playable.
I love the nature and some urban environments, but no aspect of the gameplay is enjoyable.

Fallout 4 is a game that confidently asks: "What if we took everything that made Fallout 3 great and replaced half of it with settlement building?" The answer, it turns out, is a game that is equal parts post-apocalyptic masterpiece and Sims-style housing simulator that nobody asked for.

You play as the Sole Survivor, a parent who got frozen in a vault, thawed out 200 years later, and immediately decided that the best use of your time in a radioactive wasteland is to build a roof over some settlers' heads. The game constantly reminds you that "your settlements need you," which translates to: "Stop having fun exploring and go micromanage a farm in the middle of nowhere."

The combat is serviceable, the exploration is engaging, and the story is... well, it's there. You're looking for your son, which is motivation enough until you realize that your son is a walking plot device with all the personality of a cardboard box. The factions are interesting, but choosing between them feels less like "meaningful choice" and more like "pick your favorite flavor of authoritarian government."

The real magic, though, is in the writing. The dialogue system has been "simplified" into four options that all lead to the same outcome, which is a polite way of saying "we removed player agency and called it streamlining." Listening to your character deliver voiced dialogue that you didn't write is like watching someone else play your game.

But despite all this, it's weirdly addictive. You'll spend 60 hours building settlements, collecting junk, and wondering why you're carrying 47 pounds of wood planks.

7/10. A beautiful mess that proves Bethesda doesn't understand what made their own games great, but is too charming to hate.

I played through the main questline and DLC: Far Harbor. Great ideas, combat and story. However the loading times between zones go from 30 seconds to 5 or 6 minutes. This is an unmodded game by the way. This is not normal for a ten year old game.

If you ignore the fact that Bethesda keeps pushing useless updates that break your mods to shove their shitty paid mods down your throat, or the fact that the load times are atrocious even on modern hardware, it's a great game. Except you can't ignore those, because to fix the load times you need mods, and they keep breaking them. Great work Bethesda, I'm just gonna go play New Vegas.

A shallow experience only barely saved by mods and how fun running around in power armor feels in this game at times. Vanilla content is as wide as an ocean, but with all the depth of a puddle. This is the second iteration of a Fallout game by Bethesda where we play somebody looking for a lost family member. We [i]really[/i] couldn't come up with something different here?

Get the anniversary edition when it goes on sale, I don't think it's worth full price but hey, I'm not your dad. The game is serviceable and honestly, mods will be the main thing to keep you entertained for quite some time here as the scene/community there is quite active, which is the ONLY reason this review isn't an immediate "Do Not Recommend".

The good:
-World feels interesting to explore
-Quests are (usually) unique and interesting
-Factions are all unique and have their own quirks, exploring their lore and beliefs feels rewarding in and out of the game
-One of the most visually unique games and the 1950s style has never been stronger
-The DLCs are good, Nuka World may be one of Fallout's best(i wish there wore more DLC's)
-A lot of ideas in this game could be expanded on some and be amazing in the next game
-Settlements offer the chance to shape the wasteland as you want it and allow the character to live in a variety of spots on the map

The bad:
-This game is a FPS/Looter shooter disguised as a RPG game
-Quest decisions usually don't matter, and will ultimately end in only 1-2 options with the exception of a very small handful of quests
-Creation club
-Siding with factions carries no real consequence as you can get up to almost the very last level doing every faction's questline until you have to either destroy them or complete the game with them.
-RPG game elements are non existent. I've played this game at east 10 times to completion and know of only 1-2 spots where your SPECIAL stats will allow you to make decisions, or skip quest sections
-How often your mods Break
-Your perks, SPECIAL, etc, do not effect dialogue or quests like they do in previous games
-Stability problems, as expected in any fallout game
-Lack Of Fleshed Out Dialog Options
-Bethesda
-Quests can be repetitive,…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the main story and factions as weaker or less compelling compared to previous entries in the franchise.

citations.review_text:
I returned to Fallout 4 after a while. Instead of min-maxing everything and turning the game into a checklist, I actually allowed myself to get lost in the Commonwealth.

It reminded me why I fell in love with the game, playing it for the first time on my older brother's PC when we shared a room. This is a world that's genuinely beautiful and rewards your curiosity.

The progression and perk system reward you for being thoughtful about how you develop and specialize. Settlement building actually attaches you to the idea of rebuilding. The companions are distinct, with personalities, backstories, and dialogue that make them feel alive.

The main story is pretty shallow and the factions are underdeveloped. But the atmosphere, world-building, and freedom to approach the game how you want make up for it.

They will never make me hate you Fallout 4. While the story may lack in comparison to New Vegas, this game is filled to the brim with enemies and dungeons. Every time I play i find something new. The romance options are, imo, the best of the franchise. Hancock has my heart. If you enjoy exploration and gun/melee play then this game is for you. If you want story, invent your own, idk. Main story line totally optional, imo.

get it for the mods, otherwise it's the weakest game in the franchise, the game's characters, stories and places just aren't as interesting. The game has it's high points, the gunplay is okay, the base building is jank, some characters are well written. Synths are a wasted potential, as are a lot of things in this game, even with mods it's only really enjoyable the first few playthroughs. I like it personally but I wouldn't recommend it anyone if it wasn't on sale, goos on sale all the time tho

Oh shiee.....eeeet were do I start with this slop, yes see my hours and read the words I write to you now, Fallout 4 is currently the second worst fallout game Bethesda created to exist as of 11/18/26 this can be subject to change when Todd the liar coward I mean Todd Howard releases fallout 5 in 2038. 

Fallout 4 visually and mechanically are good however the drawbacks are to much, to clarify the dialog suffered from having voiced protagonist, which made the games story super linear which is bad for a fallout game . The dialogue boils down 4 options which is yes, maybe, no and a sarcastic remark. Comparing to New Vegas to fallout 4 you have way more options in dialogue because a voice actor is not needed and you can have more options in game which lead to different and more variety of outcomes, this would also free up money for the studio to implement features from old games or to innovate and have a better story, because even developers from Bethesda said the the voice protagonist restricted them story wise which is really important in a fallout game. 

Look fallout 4 gutted the rpg mechanics and made this more of a looter shooter and settlement system that is not up to my standards, they removed the skill system and skill checks along with weapon degradation even though they had crafting mechanics for customizing guns they could've easily implement. removed karma and reputation system, also the core gameplay loop is in conflict with the main story as you are given manufactured urgency to complete the main quest, it makes the pacing bad because the game gives you the settlement feature right away which lead the player away from the story and focus on less important things that weren't implemented well. The radiant quest system was abysmal and annoying, why not have a hand craft quest instead of repetitive filler content, This kills the pacing and like I typed earlier the voiced protagonist restricted the story already so the whole tone of the game was Nagasaki-ed …

Owned this on playstation 4 for several years, and got platinum on that. Worth it to buy for my PC just to have access to better mods. First thing out of the way, the story of FO4 is -far- weaker and less robust than previous titles. But FO4 is a huge, fun sandbox to play in. The choice to make all items useful for crafting, the weapon modding system, the improved gunplay, companions, and the character development options have kept me playing this game for hundreds of hours, 114 of them on PC as of writing.

a weaker Fallout game in terms of story but all of that is completely made up for with gameplay, the settlement system, and the overall map. If you plan on playing Fallout 4 for yourself I'd suggest running it modded to fix any of those classic Bethesda bugs. Overall a solid 7/10

The writing in this game is definitely a step down from the earlier fallout games, and the voice acting from the player character is rather bad. That being said, the gameplay is simply very fun and the amount of interesting locations/details to explore in the world is a level above any other game out there. At the end, this game still holds up as a joy to play after all these years.
The story is not the best even among the Bethesda fallout games. The role playing isn't as deep and neither are the faction choices that meaningful. But its still Fallout and its addictive.

I love FO4. It's hella underrated as a game. It has so much stuff and customizability. And we're on PC so you can turn it into your own personal version of the wasteland if you want with mods. And the mods rip. You can get boob mods, and other stuff too. Is it as good as New Vegas? Fuck no. Is it fun? Yeah. Is the writing good? Moment to moment, it's great, but the overall plot is dumb as shit. Do you have choices? Hell yes you do! You can kill 3 factions and save 1. Diplomacy is for little bitches.

Would I recommend this game to other players? If you like shooting dudes in long johns, fuck yes I recommend this.

I've been playing the Fallout series since the very first game, and I've always loved both the games and the franchise as a whole. After Fallout: New Vegas, playing Fallout 4 was a genuinely enjoyable experience.

The settlement building system was exactly what I had been looking for in a Fallout game, and I ended up spending most of my playtime building and managing settlements. However, I think the vanilla experience falls quite short in several areas.

That said, there are a few things I wasn't particularly happy with. The atmosphere doesn't quite capture the bleakness and gloom of the older Fallout games. Instead, it feels more like a post-apocalyptic amusement park. The factions are also nowhere near as well-written or interesting as the ones in New Vegas.

You'll definitely have a good time with Fallout 4, but at some point, you might find yourself needing mods to get the experience you're looking for.

Fallout 4 is my favourite game of all time, while it does lack a good story partly due to it being very similar in previous entries to the franchise. Everything else is top tier, world exploration is arguably the games greatest feature. Go from point A to point B could be 10 metres away and it would take you an hour nonetheless with the shear amount of locations and lore to explore. 

Side quests is where the game shines again like other Bethesda titles. While not doing main or side quests or exploring new locations you can immerse yourself in settlement building. Probably half of my playing hours across Xbox, Playstation and PC (over 1000) would be from settlement building itself. 

Also can grab the Far Harbor DLC which is arguably one of the best Bethesda made DLCs in my opinion.

366+ Hours Later, and I'm Still Discovering an Entirely Different Game

I have over 366 hours in Fallout 4, and somehow, on my current playthrough, I'm realizing just how ridiculously MASSIVE this game actually is.

I've played through the main story before, spent hundreds of hours exploring, building settlements, completing quests, and generally hoarding every piece of junk that isn't nailed down. And yet, this playthrough feels like an entirely different experience.

The sheer amount of environmental storytelling in this game is insane.

You can walk into a random sewer looking for enough copper to build a generator and accidentally uncover an entire serial killer's story through scattered holotapes. You can investigate what seems like an ordinary location and discover disturbing secrets that have absolutely nothing to do with your active quests. You can find a random note, terminal entry, or distress signal that leads you down a rabbit hole you never knew existed.

And sometimes there's no quest marker, no achievement, and no reward. Just a genuinely fascinating story waiting for someone curious enough to piece it together.

That's what I've really come to appreciate about Fallout 4. The Commonwealth doesn't exist solely to give you quests. It feels like a world with hundreds of stories that happened long before you arrived, and Bethesda trusts you to discover them yourself.

Then there's settlement building.

OMG, settlement building.

I have spent an embarrassing amount of time scrapping entire settlements and rebuilding them into little functioning villages. I want individual houses, furnished interiors, electricity, businesses, actual jobs for settlers, and enough residents to make these places feel alive.

Unfortunately, Bethesda apparently believes a massive underground Vault should have the population of a slightly overcrowded dinner party.

The settlement-building system is simultaneously one of my favorite features and one of the most infuriating things …

The writing in this game is definitely a step down from the earlier fallout games, and the voice acting from the player character is rather bad. That being said, the gameplay is simply very fun and the amount of interesting locations/details to explore in the world is a level above any other game out there. At the end, this game still holds up as a joy to play after all these years.

Been playing on and off. The story is just ok, but i like the gameplay loop. The world has tons of POI to discover, but it could get repetitive. Mod add a whole new horizon to this game, most of my playtime is trying out different mod and starting over again.

Fallout 4 is an incredibly addictive action-RPG that delivers one of the most immersive post-apocalyptic playgrounds ever created. The post-nuclear Commonwealth of Boston is atmospheric, rich with secrets, and packed with memorable locations to explore.

The settlement system is a game-changer. Building up your own wasteland outposts, establishing trade routes, and defending your settlers adds a whole new layer of depth to the gameplay loop. Crafting armor, weapon mods, and base decorations will effortlessly swallow hours of your time.

With amazing companion characters, multiple faction storylines to choose from, and full Steam Workshop/modding support, the replayability is virtually endless.

Everything else is top tier, world exploration is arguably the games greatest feature. Go from point A to point B could be 10 metres away and it would take you an hour nonetheless with the shear amount of locations and lore to explore. 

Side quests is where the game shines again like other Bethesda titles. While not doing main or side quests or exploring new locations you can immerse yourself in settlement building. Probably half of my playing hours across Xbox, Playstation and PC (over 1000) would be from settlement building itself. 

Also can grab the Far Harbor DLC which is arguably one of the best Bethesda made DLCs in my opinion.
